title: THE YOUNG AND THE OLD ALIKE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'For a person between the ages of five and twenty, set the value of a
male at twenty shekels and of a female at ten shekels. For a person
between one month and five years, set the value of a male at five
shekels of silver and that of a female at three shekels of silver'"
- Lev 27:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The valuations included even the very young — infants of one month, and
small children. Whatever their age, they were counted. They had a place
in the vows made to God.

We should not miss what this quietly assumes: that children matter, and
that they belong within the community of God's people. In a world where
the very young were often seen as expendable, God's law counted them in.

Dear friend, Jesus made this unmistakable. When people tried to keep
children away from Him, He was indignant and said, let the little
children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God
belongs to such as these (Mark 10:14). He took them in His arms and
blessed them.

If you are raising children, you are not doing something secondary to
"real" ministry. You are shaping souls that matter eternally to God.
The tired, unseen work of nurturing a child is holy work.

And if you feel small, overlooked, or unimportant — like one of the
lowest figures on this list — remember that God's kingdom has a special
tenderness for exactly such people. Jesus said the last will be first
(Matt 20:16).

Every age, every person, counted. You are counted too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treat the nurturing of children as holy, valuable work?
2. Have I ever felt too small or unimportant to matter to God?
3. How can I bless a child or a "small" person this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You count the young, the small and the
overlooked. Help me value the people and the quiet work that the world
ignores. Amen.
